messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - unusual write activity to staging-logs bucket from service-account `svc-connector-prod` (rate spike, unusual object keys). Auto-triage flagged possible leaked debug payloads.

sre_jen: i'm on it, pulling audit logs now. which region?

incident-bot: Region: us-west-2. First anomalous object at 2026-03-17T02:17:04Z. Pattern: /tmp/debug_dump_*.log.gz

sec_mohit: tagging as security triage. initial ask: identify whether keys were exfiltrated or an internal job misconfigured. please capture last successful token issuance for that svcacct.

eng_raj: looks like a CICD job rotated yesterday. pulling pipeline history. quick grep shows `connector/publish` job ran with `svc-connector-prod` creds at 02:12 and pushed 4 files.

sre_jen: i'm pausing writes to staging-logs by adding a deny rule on the S3 policy for that principal. doing a temporary ACL block now.

sre_jen: executed: ```aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket staging-logs --policy file://deny-svc-connector.json``` response: 204

eng_raj: confirmed job still attempted push but got 403 after the policy change. good - stops further exfil.

sec_mohit: next: rotate the service-account keys used by the CICD runner and invalidate any active tokens. @oncall_tom can you rotate and force new pipeline run with new creds?

oncall_tom: starting key rotation. plan: create new access key, inject into secrets manager, update runner, then disable old key. will coordinate with eng_raj for a quick smoke.

oncall_tom: commands i'm running: ```aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-connector-prod
# update secret: aws secretsmanager put-secret-value --secret-id /ci/svc-connector-prod --secret-string '{"AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID":"...","AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY":"..."}'
# then disable old: aws iam update-access-key --user-name svc-connector-prod --access-key-id <OLD> --status Inactive
```

eng_raj: i'm watching the pipeline. when new secret injected, i'll trigger a manual build and verify artifact uploads go only to allowed prefix.

cs_maria: any customer-facing impact? did any prod customer data get included in those debug dumps?

eng_raj: initial peek: dumps contain stack traces and internal request IDs, but no PII or model payloads. looks like connector was logging request bodies for a short window. still reviewing samples.

sec_mohit: preserve the object keys for forensic ingestion. do NOT delete them yet. i'll pull copies to our secure forensic bucket.

legal_sam: pls flag anything that contains customer identifiers or tokens. if we find tokens, we'll need to rotate them and evaluate notification requirements. keep me posted.

sre_jen: forensic copy started: `aws s3 cp s3://staging-logs/tmp/ debug-preserve/ --recursive --exclude "*" --include "debug_dump_*"` - ETA ~3m

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-SVCLOGPUSH. Severity: P2. Owner: sec_mohit.

sec_mohit: summary of actions so far:
- blocked further S3 writes from svc-connector-prod
- initiated key rotation for svc-connector-prod
- pulled sample artifacts for review
- engaging legal + CS

sec_mohit: next steps: full creds audit for svcacct, rotate any tokens that show up in dumps, search for similar object patterns across other buckets, and run a quick IAM policy review on connector role (least-privilege check).

cs_maria: I'll prep a short internal blurb for affected customers if we confirm any tokens or IDs. draft to review once sec confirms.

eng_raj: pipeline smoke passed with new creds. artifacts now go to allowed prefix `ingest/ok/` only. rolling back temporary deny after monitoring confirms no further anomalies?

sre_jen: keep deny in place for 30m after rotation. monitoring alerted twice more but both attempts failed 403. looks stable.

sec_mohit: found two tokens in debug dumps that appear to be short-lived staging API tokens. no prod user tokens detected so far. will escalate if that changes.

legal_sam: good. if it's only staging tokens, notification scope is internal. continue forensic timeline and retention.

incident-bot: Update: forensic copy completed and uploaded to `forensics/INC-2026-0317-SVCLOGPUSH/`.

sre_jen: starting a sweep to detect any other principals issuing similar object key patterns across accounts: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket staging-logs --query "Contents[?contains(Key,'debug_dump_')].Key"`

sec_mohit: action items assigned: @sre_jen - bucket sweep + retention lock on preserved objects, @eng_raj - CICD credential rotation verification, @oncall_tom - confirm runner secret rotation and revoke old sessions, @cs_maria - prepare comms standby, @legal_sam - advise on notification policy.

oncall_tom: old access key set to Inactive and marked for deletion in 24h after confirming no additional usage.

eng_raj: CI run logs show no other unusual pushes. looks contained.

cs_maria: drafting internal customer note (status: contained, no production user data found, rotating staging creds) — will wait for sec_mohit signoff before sending.

sec_mohit: signing off on customer message draft. closing the active page after 2h observation. add post-incident review for root cause: debug logging got enabled by a pipeline step during a failed deploy.

sre_jen: creating a postmortem ticket and scheduling RCA. will include steps to tighten pipeline IAM and add a runtime check to disallow debug body dumps to S3.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0317-SVCLOGPUSH status -> Contained. Clocked start: 1750009876.

sre_jen: leaving the channel, follow-ups tracked in INC ticket. :white_check_mark:
